headline: In Nepal and Tibet, floods triggered by ice-rock avalanche bring devastation
subhead: Floods and mudslides of unprecedented violence, brought on by the collapse of a high-altitude glacier, have buried villages and roads, killing at least 180 people and leaving more than 1,300 missing as of Thursday. The affected region is popular with trekkers and Hindu pilgrims.

Car ramming in Normandy leaves two dead, nine injured
subhead: Two people died and nine were injured after a man drove a car into a group of people in the city of Caen in France's northwest Normandy region on Wednesday. Police said they believe the incident occurred after a fight and did not have a terrorist motive.

headline: Gulf countries seek new routes for 'black gold' to free themselves from the Strait of Hormuz
subhead: Pipeline projects are taking shape to allow the region's oil powers to move their production after six months of heightened tensions between Tehran and Washington.

headline: 'After a summer of heatwaves and fires, awareness remains low and preparedness is virtually nonexistent'
subhead: Environmental historian Judith Rainhorn criticizes France's political leaders for their inability to respond to the climate emergency, saying that it is time to 'politicize the disasters weighing us down.'

headline: How a tenacious French diplomat undertook the monumental construction of the Suez Canal
subhead: 'Suez, a historic canal' (2/6). Efforts to connect the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea followed one after another from antiquity onward. But it was not until the arrival of Ferdinand de Lesseps – who was neither a scientist nor an engineer – that the project became a reality.

subhead: With just three months to go before the building permit for the transformation of the Paris skyscraper expires, a series of unexpected twists has shaken the project launched a decade ago. In July, Paris Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire urged the co-owners to settle their disputes. Le Monde takes a look behind the scenes at the ongoing negotiations.

headline: Soldier testimony sheds light on how Israel wages information war
subhead: One year after the bombing that killed 22 people, including five journalists, at Nasser Hospital in the south of the Gaza Strip, an Israeli soldier has told several media outlets, including Le Monde, how the Israeli army pulls out all stops to link bombing victims to Hamas.

headline: Want to escape heatwaves? These are the best places to buy property in France
subhead: Climate concerns are increasingly becoming a key factor when buying an apartment or house. Coastal areas and those at higher altitudes, thought to be better protected from extreme heat, are particularly attractive to potential buyers.
